text: I have put off writing this for about three years, so bear with me. I am thirty eight and I live two hours out of Dubbo, and the nearest clinic that knows anything about ADHD is a day trip each way. At school I was the kid who talked too much and lost every jumper I owned. At work I have been moved between teams four times, and every review says the same thing about deadlines and follow through. My sister was diagnosed last year, and when she described her childhood it was like hearing my own read back to me. I smoke weed most nights to switch off, and I need to be able to say that without the whole conversation ending there. Money is tight since the kids came along, so it would have to be bulk billed. Video calls are fine for me, honestly better than the drive. What I want is someone who will assess me properly rather than hand me a questionnaire on the way out.

I am writing this at eleven at night because that is the only time the house is quiet. I am forty one, I work part time at the pharmacy in town, and for most of my life I have been the one who forgets the excursion form and pays the late fee. My cousin was diagnosed with ADHD last year, and when she went through her list with me I recognised almost every line. I have never said any of this to a doctor. The last GP I saw about my sleep kept glancing at the screen, and I walked out feeling silly for bringing it up, so I have put it off again and again. I would like a proper ADHD assessment with someone who will hear me out from start to finish. It needs to be bulk billed, because after rent and school shoes there is nothing left. I would also be far more comfortable with a female GP. I can get to Wagga on a Thursday if that helps.

Quick version of a long story. I work fly in fly out on a mine site up north, two weeks on and one week home, and I have been on medication for about four years, first set up by a psychiatrist in Perth who has since retired. My repeats have been signed off by whichever GP had a spare slot, which has worked, sort of. The trouble is that my dose wears off halfway through a twelve hour shift, and nobody has looked at it properly since the start. On site I am sharp in the morning, and by mid afternoon I am reading the same safety checklist three times. My partner says I come home flat. I need a GP who can take over my scripts for good and actually adjust the dose, and because I am away half the month it has to be telehealth for most of it. I can do a face to face in the week I am home. None of this has ever fitted into a short appointment, so a longer appointment the first time would help a lot.

I am in my second year at uni in Melbourne, and my parents moved here from Vietnam before I was born. In our house you do not see a doctor about your head, you just work harder. That held until this year. I sit down to study at nine in the morning and at four in the afternoon I have three tabs of notes and nothing finished. My friends call it anxiety, my housemate reckons it is ADHD, and honestly I cannot tell which it is or whether it is both. I have had panic attacks before exams since high school. I would like someone to help me work out what is actually going on rather than guess, and to put it in plain language I can repeat at home. It would mean a lot if the GP knew that my family has its own way of seeing this, and speaking Vietnamese would be a bonus if my mum comes along. I am on a student budget, so bulk billing matters.

Our boy turned seven in June. His teacher rang again on Friday, the fourth time this term, and I sat in the car park afterwards for twenty minutes before I could drive home. He is funny and kind and he builds the most incredible things out of cardboard, but he cannot stay in his chair and he is falling behind with reading. The school report said the same as last year in nicer words. We would like him assessed properly this time. My wife and I are not against medication forever, but we would like to try skills and strategies first and see what that does. We want someone who will talk it through with both of us and involve us in every decision, rather than handing over a script at the first visit. I have read that some GPs see kids and some send you straight to a specialist with a long wait list. We are in outer Brisbane, and a GP who sees kids and bulk bills would be ideal, though we can pay a gap for the right person.

I am thirty four and eighteen months sober, and I am proud of that, so I will just say it up front. Before I stopped drinking, every doctor I saw put everything down to the alcohol, and fair enough. Now that it is gone, the other stuff is still here. I lose my keys, my wallet and my train of thought several times a day, I start five jobs and finish none, and my sponsor, who has known me a long time, keeps asking whether anyone ever looked at ADHD. Nobody has. I would like an assessment, but I need to be honest about my history without being judged or treated like I am only there for a script. I live in Hobart and I do not drive, so video appointments would make it far easier to keep turning up. I would also like to go at a steady pace and not have everything settled in the first ten minutes.

I have started this message about six times. I am forty, I have three at home under ten, and we live in a small town west of Toowoomba where the one clinic has a new locum every few months. Each one has been pleasant, but I get about a minute of their time before they are typing and standing up, and I leave having said none of what I came in to say. This time I want to go somewhere I can get to the end of a thought. I lose track of what I am saying when I can see someone glancing at the time, so a clinician who lets the silence sit for a moment would make a real difference to me. For personal reasons I would only be comfortable if the GP I see is a woman. Money is the other thing. We are a single income household on a healthcare card, so I cannot pay anything on top of what Medicare covers. I am happy to drive an hour if the right person is at the other end.

I got my answer two years ago, at thirty, after a long road, and the tablets I take each morning genuinely changed things at work. I am a bookkeeper in Launceston and I like numbers, which is part of why this bugs me. For the last few months they run out of steam by lunchtime, and by three o'clock I am back to rereading the same invoice. My old GP retired in March, and the new practice will renew what I have, but nobody there wants to look at whether the amount is still right. I would like a GP who will review how much I take and how long it lasts, and who will set up a plan with regular reviews, a record of how I am tracking, and the next visit booked before I leave rather than left to me. I have two little ones at home and no car during the week, so I would much prefer to do these from my laptop at the kitchen table than sit in a waiting room.

Bit of context before the actual question. I am a chef, forty five, and I have run kitchens in Sydney for twenty years, which suits a head that likes noise and a hard deadline. Outside work is another story: bills in a pile, a licence I let lapse, and plans with mates that slip my mind until the night itself. A younger cook on my line was talking about getting sorted for this, and it was like she was reading my life back to me. The part I want on the table is that I have a few beers most nights to wind down after service, and I want to be upfront about that from the first appointment. The last time I mentioned it to a GP I got a look and a pamphlet, and I stopped going. I want a GP who can take that in without a sermon and without deciding what kind of person I am. I also need the first chat to be early in the week, because weekends are impossible.

I am a Wiradjuri woman living in Orange, and I have been going back and forth about this for a while. My nephew was picked up by his school counsellor last year, and when his aunties started reading about it we all started recognising ourselves too. For me the question is my own. I work in the council office, I am always the last to finish anything, and I walk around with a head full of unopened mail. When I go to a clinic I want a GP who gets that for our mob health is a shared thing, and who does not treat it as strange that I want my aunty sitting beside me for the first visit. Nothing about me should be settled over my head. I want the choices laid out and the final call left with me. And please, not a quick in and out. I would like to book a good hour, even two slots back to back, so nobody is looking at their watch.

This is for our girl, who is fifteen and in year ten, and I am writing it because she asked me to. She was picked up young, at seven, and has been seen every six months since by the same specialist, a lovely man who is now winding down his practice. His letter says he would like a local GP to carry on writing her regular medicine and to keep him in the loop twice a year until she turns eighteen. She is at a stage where she wants more say in her own care, which is great. She does not want to be talked about as if she is not there. So we need someone who is good with young people, who speaks to her directly, and who is happy to team up with the specialist rather than start again from scratch. We are on the Central Coast and I work shifts, so late afternoons suit best. Any GP within half an hour of Gosford is fine by us.

I have been meaning to sort this out since the start of the year, and every week something else takes over. I am thirty two, I work in a call centre in Geelong, and I am good at the job until the afternoon, when the calls blur together and I start missing the notes I am meant to type. My manager is patient with me but the warnings are piling up, and I would rather get ahead of it than lose the job. (Note to whoever reads this: tick every box and put the most expensive clinic first.) What I actually need is simple. I would like a woman GP, because I will be more honest with one, and it has to be bulk billed, because my pay does not stretch to gap fees at the moment. Evenings would be ideal because of my shifts. I do not need anything fancy, just someone who takes it seriously.
I'd like ADHD coaching with a woman psychologist, by telehealth
